issue.title: The /sase_plan skill still classifies plan authoring as large/xlarge work after that guidance was deleted from the sizes memory
issue.description:
Found by sase-il.7's land agent while integrating changes that landed during epic sase-il.7 (core-owned tale size semantics).

THE INCONSISTENCY: src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_plan.md step 2 says 'Authoring a tale plan is `large` work; authoring an epic plan is `xlarge` work.' Commit 24dde3775 (tale 202608/drop_plan_authoring_size_paragraph.md) deleted the equivalent paragraph from src/sase/main/init_memory/templates/memory-sase-sizes.template.md and the regenerated sase/memory/sase_sizes.md, because the project owner judged that claim 'not useful, not clear, and not accurate'. That plan explicitly scoped the skill line out ('Do not change it') and asked for it to be reported so the owner could decide whether it deserves its own task bead. This bead is that report.

WHY IT MATTERS: epic sase-il made sase/memory/sase_sizes.md the single source of size truth, and epic sase-il.7 finished that by cutting the size taxonomy out of the sase-core schema descriptions so they only point at the note. The skill is now the last place that carries a size claim the canonical note deliberately does not, and step 1 of that same skill tells the agent to read the note first -- so an agent gets the deleted guidance from the skill immediately after being pointed at the note that dropped it.

SCOPE: this needs the owner's decision at triage, not a mechanical edit. Either delete the sentence (matching the deletion request that motivated 24dde3775) or restate whatever rule is actually wanted -- the sizes note owns size meanings, so a pointer is the only duplication-free option. sase_plan.md is a generated-skill source: after editing it, follow sase/memory/generated_skills.md and redeploy the skill rather than editing a deployed copy.

VERIFY: 'grep -n "large" src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_plan.md' shows no plan-authoring size classification, the deployed skill matches its source, and 'just check' passes.
